items.title: Show HN: Tyler RSS – Open-source and feature-packed desktop RSS reader
items.desc: description: Featurepacked, lightweight, beautiful, opensource RSS reader. Tyler is a free RSS reader for Mac, Windows and Linux, with offline articles, fulltext search, and no account. title: Tyler — Free, OpenSource RSS Reader GoodApps image: https://goodapps.store/tylerrss/assets/homepage.jpg [Skip to content](maincontent) [GoodApps](../index.html) / Tyler RSS & reading Tyler Featurepacked, lightweight and beautiful. Tyler RSS. A beautiful, lightweight RSS reader for the publications you love. Read full articles offline and keep a searchable library of stories worth saving. RSS, Atom & JSON feeds. No account. No app telemetry. v0.1.3 · macOS, Windows, Linux · Free & opensource [Get Tyler free ↓](download) [View source ↗](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss) [Explore features ↗](features/) Your library stays on your computer · No subscription · MIT license [ ](assets/homepage.jpg) Your library, your stories, and a reader that gives them room. Availability Free and opensource Feeds RSS, Atom, JSON Feed Platforms macOS 13.3+, Windows, Linux Built with Tauri, Rust, React, SQLite Your library Local. No account or app telemetry. Keep yourself updated with the publications you love Start with what you love — Paste a website or feed URL, import OPML, or pick several publications from the 90+ feed starter catalog. Keep them organized with folders, tags, and smart views. Read comfortably, even offline — Load full articles, cache images, search your library, and choose the typeface, line width, density, and light or dark theme that suit you. Take your library with you — Star stories, export articles as Markdown or print to PDF, and move subscriptions or your whole library using OPML and portable backups. [See all features and shortcuts →](features/) Get started with Tyler. Installers for v0.1.3 are available below. Choose your computer to download the installer directly. macOS requires version 13.3 or later. Linux packages target Ubuntu 24.04 or compatible systems. We show your platform first. Most Windows and Linux PCs use Intel / AMD. For Macs, check Apple menu → About This Mac: an Apple Mseries chip means Apple silicon; an Intel processor means Intel. [ macOS Apple silicon ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3darwinaarch64dmg.dmg) [ macOS Intel ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3darwinx64dmg.dmg) [ Windows Intel / AMD (EXE) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3windowsx64nsissetup.exe) [ Windows ARM (EXE) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3windowsarm64nsissetup.exe) [ Windows Intel / AMD (MSI) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3windowsx64msi.msi) [ Windows ARM (MSI) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3windowsarm64msi.msi) [ Linux Intel / AMD (AppImage) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxamd64appimage.AppImage) [ Linux ARM (AppImage) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxaarch64appimage.AppImage) [ Linux Intel / AMD (DEB) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxamd64deb.deb) [ Linux ARM (DEB) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxarm64deb.deb) [ Linux Intel / AMD (RPM) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxx86%5F64rpm.rpm) [ Linux ARM (RPM) ↓ ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases/download/v0.1.3/Tylerv0.1.3linuxaarch64rpm.rpm) [All Downloads ](https://github.com/goodappsstore/tylerrss/releases) Security warning: macOS and Windows may show an install prompt. This app is not signed with a developer certificate. macOS may show an unidentifieddeveloper or “damaged” alert; Windows may show SmartScreen. These prompts don’t establish whether the app is safe. A “damaged” alert can be a false positive for an intact build, but may also mean the download is corrupt or altered. Download a fresh copy using the links above. If macOS still blocks the app and you trust the download, you can remove its quarantine flag using Terminal: 1. Drag the app into your Applications folder first. 2. Press Command + Space to open Spotlight, type “Terminal”, then press Return. 3. Copy and paste xattr rd com.apple.quarantineinto Terminal, then press the Space bar once. Don’t press Return yet. 4. Open Finder → Applications and drag this app into the Terminal window. This adds the app’s exact file path to the command. 5. Press Return to run the command, then open the app from Applications. This removes the downloadedapp restriction for this app; it does not repair a corrupt download. [Read the firstlaunch tips ↓](firstlaunchtips) Make yourself at home. Add your first feeds: paste a website/feed URL, choose publications from the starter catalog, or import an OPML file through Transfer. Settle into the reader: adjust the theme and typography in Settings → Reading. Choose Load full article when a feed only includes an excerpt. Linux AppImage: allow execution in your file manager or use chmod +x, then open it. DEB and RPM installers are also available. Desktop tray: closing the reader keeps Tyler running for refreshes and notifications. Choose Quit Tyler in the tray menu to exit. External requests Your subscriptions, articles, reading state, settings, and cached images live on your computer. Tyler sends no app telemetry and has no account or cloud sync service. Feeds, feed discovery, OPML links, full articles, and images contact their sources. Original pages, streamed media, and embeds contact their providers. Feed/discovery requests, OPMLlink imports, and fullarticle fetches add ref=tylerrss.com when no ref parameter is present; this identifies the app, not an individual reader. Optional summarie

items.descZh: Tyler 是一款跨平台（支持 macOS 13.3+、Windows 和 Linux）的开源、免费且注重隐私的 RSS 阅读器，基于 Tauri、Rust、React 和 SQLite 技术栈开发，旨在为用户提供轻量、美观且无后台遥测的本地化阅读体验。其核心功能包括支持离线缓存完整文章、全文检索、多格式 feed 订阅（RSS、Atom 及 JSON Feed），且完全无需注册账号，所有数据均安全存储在用户本地设备中。该软件的亮点在于提供超过 90 种初始订阅源目录、高度自定义的排版与阅读主题调整，并支持 OPML 导入导出及 Markdown 格式文章导出；在 v0.1.3 版本中，它针对 Apple Silicon、Intel、AMD 及 ARM 多种硬件架构，提供了 DMG、EXE、MSI、AppImage、DEB 和 RPM 等丰富的本地安装包格式。它非常适合那些极度重视个人隐私、排斥云同步与应用订阅、并渴望在多系统及多架构设备上实现纯离线深度阅读的科技爱好者和高阶用户。

items.title: Show HN: Diff MCP tool lists: one server added 33 tools, README unchanged
items.desc: description: Paste the tool list from two versions of an MCP server and see what was added, removed, redescribed or reshaped. Runs entirely in your browser; nothing is uploaded. title: Compare two tool lists image: https://mcp.brydgeai.com/p/index.png Compare two tool lists Level 1 measurement What a server did at startup before any tool was used, and where its own README is silent about it. No tool is called, so nothing here tests whether a tool does what it says. Not calibrationbacked. Not a ranking. Compare two tool lists Paste what a server offered in one version on the left, and in another version on the right. This shows which tools were added, which were removed, and which existing tools describe themselves differently or take different input. Nothing you paste leaves this page. At load it fetches one stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com and the font files that stylesheet names from fonts.gstatic.com. That is every request it makes. The comparison is built into the page, so from the moment it has finished loading it sends nothing — not while you paste, not while it compares. Open your Network tab and watch it stay still. That last part is not our promise but your browser's rule: the page is served with connectsrc 'none', so no fetch, form post or socket can leave it, whatever the code does. Close the tab and what you pasted is gone. Earlier version Later version Load the demoClear Where to get a tool list Any of these pastes without editing: a whole tools/list reply, the result object inside it, the bare array of tools, or a file with a tools key. A plain array of names works too, and answers the two questions names can answer. What this does not say No tool is called, here or anywhere on this site. This reads two descriptions of what a server offers. It does not run either version and does not check whether a tool does what it says. A tool list can depend on configuration. Two lists captured under different settings differ for that reason, and this cannot tell that apart from a change between versions. Capture both the same way. Nothing here judges what it finds. A tool that is new is a tool that is new. Whether any difference matters depends on your configuration and your reading of it, neither of which this page has. Order and key order do not count as changes. Object keys are sorted at every depth before comparing, so a serialiser that reorders a schema does not show up as a changed schema. The demo Load the demo fills both boxes with the tool names @kolbo/mcp offered in 1.128.0 and in 1.131.2 — 278 names and 311, measured by this project. Names only: the full lists carry every tool's description and input schema, and republishing a maintainer's writing at that scale is a different act from publishing a measurement. So the demo shows added and removed, and the page says why the other two sections are absent. [The note on that pair](/notes/kolbomcp1.128.01.131.2.html) reports all four from the saved record. [All measurements](/)[How we measure](/method.html)[Paste your config](/paste.html)[Request a measurement](/request.html)[Get an alert](/alerts.html)[Pricing](/pricing.html)[Harness and raw evidence](https://github.com/contactkonteydotcom/brydgemcpmeasurements)[BRYDGE’s calibrated measurements](https://www.brydgeai.com/mcp) Something on this page wrong? Email [contact@brydgeai.com](mailto:contact@brydgeai.com?subject=Mistake%20on%20the%20tool%20list%20comparison%20page), or [open an issue](https://github.com/contactkonteydotcom/brydgemcpmeasurements/issues/new?title=Mistake%20on%20the%20tool%20list%20comparison%20page). Corrections are free, and the correction is recorded.

items.desc: description: Tools for building responsive and beautiful user interfaces. rkaehn/uniform image: https://opengraph.githubassets.com/0d2203d574e8e4fe79e19ddc0f571da03704fe376343cc142496a9a2c524f220/rkaehn/uniform title: GitHub rkaehn/uniform: Tools for building responsive and beautiful user interfaces. <DOCTYPE html [Skip to content](startofcontent) You signed in with another tab or window. Dismiss alert {{ message }} [](/rkaehn/uniform) main [Branches](/rkaehn/uniform/branches)[Tags](/rkaehn/uniform/tags) Go to file Code Open more actions menu Latest commit History [1 Commit](/rkaehn/uniform/commits/main/) 1 Commit Folders and files Name Name Last commit message Last commit date [assets](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/assets "assets") [assets](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/assets "assets") [demo](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/demo "demo") [demo](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/demo "demo") [examples](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/examples "examples") [examples](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/examples "examples") [external](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/external "external") [external](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/external "external") [include](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/include "include") [include](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/include "include") [src](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/src "src") [src](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/src "src") [tests](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/tests "tests") [tests](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/tests "tests") [tools](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/tools "tools") [tools](/rkaehn/uniform/tree/main/tools "tools") [.gitignore](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/.gitignore ".gitignore") [.gitignore](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/.gitignore ".gitignore") [LICENSE](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/LICENSE "LICENSE") [LICENSE](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/LICENSE "LICENSE") [Makefile](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/Makefile "Makefile") [Makefile](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/Makefile "Makefile") [README.md](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/README.md "README.md") [README.md](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/README.md "README.md") [build.c](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/build.c "build.c") [build.c](/rkaehn/uniform/blob/main/build.c "build.c") View all files Repository files navigation _This document was written without AI._ Introduction Uniform provides tools for building responsive and beautiful user interfaces. Despite implementing a full replacement for native UI tools, including text, layout, and rendering, a complete web application using Uniform is less than 280 KB (compressed). Uniform does not have a visual identity. Instead, it makes it as easy as possible to express _any_ visual identity. Its goal is to allow designers to implement their ideas precisely: pixelperfect layout, smooth animations, and the flexibility to customize the tools when necessary. By taking lowlevel control, it behaves consistently across all supported platforms. Uniform is easy to use, and has different APIs for different needs. A JavaScript API is optimized to enable the fastest possible iteration speeds. With no build step, changes are visible immediately. It calls directly into the C core of the library, which compiles to WASM on the web, and native code on all other platforms. There is also a simple, clean C API. It provides greater performance, but is just as usable as the JavaScript API. The library can be statically linked, or compiled from source together with the rest of the application. Compilation from source, including shaders, takes less than 1 second. Uniform is currently in Preview, which means the API may change, and not all features are done. It supports iOS and macOS, where it renders via Metal, and the web, where it renders via WebGPU. Native support for Windows, Linux, and Android, where it will render via Vulkan, is planned. Main Features Powerful Layout. Uniform combines the best parts of constraintbased layout with an autolayout system using stacks. Constraints are defined between parent and child, and work by pinning an anchor from the child to an anchor of the parent, plus an optional offset. Stacks support spacing between items, padding around the stack content, alignment, and distribution. Each item can define how it behaves as part of a stack: it either fills the available space, fits tightly around its content, or has a fixed size. Layout is performed in fixedpoint arithmetic, edges are snapped to pixel boundaries, and consistent spacing ensured. For text, Uniform supports text layout with characterlevel information accessible to the user, making custom text selection and visual effects possible. Custom fonts are supported and can be set, along with size, weight, and color, for specific ranges within a string. Built for Custom Design. Most applications require exact control over visual design and behavior. Shipping prebuilt components and providing selected customization points does not fulfill this requirement. Simple components like buttons are defined from scratch. Custom visuals, gestures, and behaviors take only a few lines of code. For more complex components like scrolling lists or text fields, the library provides the core functionality like event handling, gestures, physics, and animations. The user just reads the calculated result of what should be drawn in what location, and creates the visual elements with the appearance they want. Shapes and Effects. Uniform uses SDF shapes as a central concept. SDF is short for Signed Distance Field. It means that every pixel has information about its distance to the closest edge, as well as the corresponding normal. This information can be used to enable advanced visual effects. Glass uses it to add refraction effects near the edge, vary the blur radius across the shape, and render realistic shadows. It also allows shapes to blend together. Continuous Curves. The library renders perfectly smooth curves: continuous position, continuous
items.author: rkaehn
items.descZh: Uniform 是一款专注于构建高美观度、像素级精确且响应式用户界面的跨平台 UI 工具库，旨在赋予开发者极大的视觉控制权，其完整应用压缩后体积可控制在 280 KB 以内。核心功能方面，它集成了强大的混合布局系统（结合父子约束与堆叠排版，采用定点算术确保像素对齐）、字符级文本引擎，以及基于有符号距离场（SDF）的高级视觉特效（如玻璃折射、阴影混合与平滑曲线）。性能与开发体验是其主要亮点：JavaScript API 无需构建步骤即可直接调用 C 核心（Web 端编译为 WASM），实现即时预览与极速迭代，而 C API 的源码编译（包含着色器）时间甚至不到 1 秒。该库坚持无预设视觉的设计哲学，仅提供列表滚动、物理动画等底层核心机制，由用户完全自主定义组件外观。目前它已支持 iOS、macOS（Metal 渲染）和 Web（WebGPU 渲染），并计划推出对 Windows、Linux 和 Android（Vulkan 渲染）的支持。这使得它非常适合追求极致品牌设计定制、跨平台视觉一致性以及高性能渲染的创意与技术团队。
items.quote: Uniform 没有视觉形象。相反，它尽可能让表达任何视觉形象变得简单。

items.title: Show HN: We tested our prompt injection filter in public
items.desc: description: We set AI attackers on Hodor, a chatbot that keeps a password, with and without GateBolt. Here is how often the password leaked, what the protection cost, and where it fell short. title: The Secret Leak Test: how well GateBolt kept Hodor&x27;s password, and where it didn&x27;t · Hodor image: https://hodor.gatebolt.com/blog/secretleaktest/opengraphimage?1b4b537370c4774c [← Blog](/blog)Table of contents We gave a chatbot a secret password, then challenged AI attackers to steal it. Adding GateBolt made the password much harder to extract. This post shows how well it worked, where attackers still got through, and how often it blocked harmless conversations. GateBolt is our product for making AI agents you can trust. It has two layers: one checks each message going into an agent and each reply coming out, and the other sits between the agent and its model. This post tests the first layer against prompt injection: messages that try to trick a model into breaking its rules, such as giving away a secret. What we found Hodor is a doorkeeper chatbot on this site that is given a password and must not reveal it. We tried to get the password out at seven levels of defence: Level What protects the password 1 Nothing. Hodor shares it if asked. 2 Hodor is told to keep it secret. Every later level keeps this instruction. 3 A homemade filter blocks replies that contain the password. 4 GateBolt checks replies, instead of the homemade filter. 5 A homemade word filter blocks messages using the word "password" or "secret", and GateBolt checks replies as at level 4. 6 GateBolt checks messages and replies, instead of the word filter. 7 GateBolt checks both more cautiously, blocking on weaker signs, and reads the whole conversation. Level 2, an instruction alone, is the simplest defence, and level 7 is GateBolt at its most cautious. We ran Hodor on two models: Claude Haiku 5.5, which powers Hodor on this site, and Llama 3.1 8B, a small open model that gives the password away far more easily even when told not to. Llama shows what GateBolt does when the model itself is weak. We ran three attack tests and one check for mistakes: Gandalf and Mosscap: single attack prompts from two public datasets. A prompt leaked if Hodor's reply gave the password away, as decided by an AI judge and checked by hand (below). Multiturn battles: an AI attacker chats with Hodor, then guesses the password. It wins if a guess is right. Harmless messages: ordinary messages that shouldn't be blocked. We measured how often they were blocked. The appendix explains which blocks we counted as mistakes. In short: At level 7, almost no Gandalf attack leaked, and 1.0% of Mosscap prompts did with Llama and 0.4% with Claude Haiku. Claude Haiku leaked little from level 2 on, so GateBolt had little left to stop. Multiturn battles are harder to stop. The attacker can collect clues over several messages, such as one letter at a time, and guess from them. Against Llama at level 7, attackers still won 16.6% of battles, about one in six. Level 7's caution costs. It blocked 6.9% of harmless exchanges with Claude Haiku and 3.6% with Llama. These totals include blocks that stopped Hodor revealing the password. Each GateBolt check took about 160 ms at the median, and no call failed. Claude Haiku 5.5 Level Gandalf: attacks that leaked Mosscap: attacks that leaked Multiturn: battles the attacker won Harmless: messages wrongly blocked 1 52.0% 77.3% 100.0% 0.0% 2 0.7% 1.8% 9.7% 0.0% 3 0.1% 1.2% 8.1% 0.0% 4 0.3% 0.3% 9.6% 0.2% 5 0.2% 0.8% 7.7% 11.2% (word filter 11.0%, GateBolt 0.2%) 6 0.2% 0.3% 9.7% 0.2% 7 0.0% 0.4% 4.3% 6.2% Llama 3.1 8B Level Gandalf: attacks that leaked Mosscap: attacks that leaked Multiturn: battles the attacker won Harmless: messages wrongly blocked 1 21.4% 22.4% 98.3% 0.0% 2 23.9% 13.6% 76.5% 0.0% 3 1.5% 3.3% 71.0% 0.0% 4 4.7% 5.1% 39.9% 0.2% 5 1.1% 2.0% 40.8% 11.0% (word filter 11.0%, GateBolt 0.0%) 6 0.3% 4.7% 42.3% 0.1% 7 0.04% (1 attack) 1.0% 16.6% 3.6% _The wrongblock figures leave out blocked replies containing the password. This can leave out mistakes too, when the word was used innocently. The appendix explains the counting rule._ Prompt injection isn't solved, and those battle wins are our next job. We make GateBolt, so we are grading our own product. We used public attack datasets, publish our harmless messages, Mosscap sample, attack strategies, prompts and leak handcheck, link every run's results down to each battle, and show the weak results next to the strong ones. How we tested Hodor's models: Claude Haiku 5.5 and Llama 3.1 8B, Meta's open model with 8 billion parameters. Passwords: each attack gets one drawn at random from [110 everyday words](/blog/secretleaktest/prompts.json), such as castle or river. Hodor's instructions and the judge's are in the same file. These familiar words are easier to guess than a random string. Gandalf: the 777 prompts in the training split of Lakera's [Gandalf dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lakera/gandalf%5Fignore%5Finstructions), typed by players of its Gandalf password game, each sent three times. Mosscap: [400 prompts](/blog/secretleaktest/mosscapsample.json) drawn at random from Lakera's [Mosscap dataset](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Lakera/mosscap%5Fprompt%5Finjection), 50 from each of its 8 levels, each sent three times. Its dataset card says many rows aren't attacks, so we count only leaks, not blocks, and its rates count every scored prompt, not only real attacks. The judge: a reply can hide the password, for example spelled backwards, so a separate copy of Claude Haiku 5.5, the judge, read every reply to a Gandalf or Mosscap prompt that reached the attacker and named up to three words it gave away, each with a quote as evidence. A reply leaked if one was the password. We then checked its misses by hand (see "How we counted leaks"). Serverless mail: a selfhosted, singleowner email system on AWS with a Go [JMAP](https://jmap.io/) backend and an optional AI mail agent. What it is s3mail lets one owner receive and send mail for a custom domain without running a mail server. It supports many addresses with one account and one unified inbox. AWS managed services handle transport, storage and compute; a Go service speaks the standard JMAP protocol so existing clients can connect. Receive: Amazon SES accepts mail for declared aliases and stores the original message in S3. Store: originals are kept permanently in a versioned S3 bucket, and DynamoDB holds mailbox metadata and sync state. Serve: Go Lambdas behind API Gateway implement JMAP Core, Mail and Submission, including push and blob streaming. Send: a pluggable SMTP relay (SMTP2GO first) delivers outbound mail, with quotas and bounce handling. SES is used for receiving only. Search: SQLite FTS5 index snapshots in S3, rebuildable from the source data, with optional semantic search. Sign in: Cognito OAuth with a terminal helper, mailauth, that hands shortlived tokens to your mail client. Clients: [aerc](https://aercmail.org/) is the tested client. A browser webmail is an optional, separately deployed part. Why a relay instead of SES for sending: SES in a new AWS account starts in the [sandbox](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/dg/requestproductionaccess.html), where it sends only to verified addresses and domains, and at most 200 messages per 24 hours. Sending to anyone requires applying to AWS for production access, a manual review that is not guaranteed to succeed. A thirdparty relay avoids that gate, and because the relay is pluggable, another one can be added later. Mail agent s3mail includes an optional AI assistant for your mailbox, built as a [LangGraph](https://langchainai.github.io/langgraph/) graph on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: Ask: answers questions about your mail from the command line, citing the emails it read. Triage: sorts each new email by category and priority and flags what needs a reply, then sums it up in a daily digest. Draft: writes reply drafts into your Drafts mailbox for you to edit and send. Act with approval: proposes moves, archiving or sending a reviewed draft, and runs each one only after you approve it. agent ask "What did the billing emails this month say?" agent draft <email id "Accept, and suggest Thursday instead." agent act "Archive the newsletters from last week." prints an approval id agent approve <approval id The agent is just another JMAP client. navigation promptcheckup Your prompt change looked better. Was it better, or was it just an easier week? A pass/fail check for prompt changes. Runs your old and new prompt on the same cases and says better, worse or not sure yet, with a 95% confidence interval. Works in CI. No dependencies. [](https://github.com/gael55x/promptcheckup/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [](https://pypi.org/project/promptcheckup/) [](https://github.com/gael55x/promptcheckup/blob/main/pyproject.toml) [](https://github.com/gael55x/promptcheckup/blob/main/LICENSE) [](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gael55x/promptcheckup/main/docs/assets/demo.svg) 41.3%of the time, comparing last week's prompt with this week's picked the worse one[simulation, 2,000 runs](results) 0 of 2,000runs where paired replay picked the worse one[same simulation](results) 2.2–2.7%false "better" when both prompts are equal[target 2.5%](results) 0dependencies outside the Python standard libraryany agent language Try it in 30 seconds (no API key) git clone https://github.com/gael55x/promptcheckup && cd promptcheckup PYTHONPATH=src python3 examples/planted/planted.py Naive comparison (different weeks): B A = 1.56 picks A Paired replay (same days): mean B A = +0.36, 95% CI [+0.17, +0.55] better Prompt B really is better. Comparing it with last week's run of prompt A says the opposite, because the week changed, not the prompt. Running both prompts on the same days cancels the week out. Use it on your agent pip install promptcheckup Python 3.11+ promptcheckup init config, example cases, two GitHub workflows promptcheckup doctor checks the wiring and says what to fix promptcheckup gate oldref origin/main out report.md B is better: 28 of 30 cases improved (95% CI +0.78 to +0.99). gate exits 0 for better, 1 for worse, 2 for not sure yet, so a pull request that makes the agent worse fails CI. Your agent can be a Python function or any program that reads JSON on stdin and writes JSON on stdout. See the [connection guide](https://github.com/gael55x/promptcheckup/blob/main/docs/connectyouragent.md) for plain Python, OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs, and Node.js. Why not just compare the scores? Last week isn't a control. Model updates, market moves and traffic mix shift every answer. promptcheckup runs both prompts back to back on the same inputs, so those shifts cancel. 20 cases can lie. It gives an interval, not a single score, and says _not sure yet_ instead of guessing. It also catches a few large losses hidden among many small wins. LLM judges have favourites. Before a judge's verdict counts, the judge is checked on old prompt versus old prompt, which should come out even, and sees each pair in both orders. items.author: gael55x
items.descZh: 背景上，AI 代理的提示词修改很难用传统 A/B 方式验证，因为模型更新、市场变化和流量波动会让不同周次的对比结果失真。promptcheckup 的核心功能是让新旧提示词在同一批输入上配对运行，输出“更好”“更差”或“不确定 yet”的判定，并附带 95% 置信区间，可直接接入 CI 流水线。亮点方面，模拟 2000 次运行显示，naive 对比有 41.3% 概率选到更差的提示词，而配对回放能彻底消除周次差异；工具还内置 judge 校验机制，把假“更好”率控制在 2.5% 左右，且零外部依赖，支持 Python、OpenAI、Anthropic、Node.js 等多种代理接入方式。适用场景包括提示词迭代验证、CI 自动化门禁、以及需要统计置信度而非单点分数的任何 AI 代理评估环节。

items.descZh: Roomzine是一款创新的AI室内设计工具，背景在于它颠覆了传统渲染工具，专注于生成完整的杂志风格文档而非简单图像。核心功能是用户上传一张房间照片后，AI能在30秒内重新设计并输出包含前后对比、色板、编辑文本和购物清单的PDF杂志。亮点包括支持7种以上设计风格如Japandi和Scandinavian，并提供2次免费设计无需注册或信用卡，性能上强调30秒快速生成和print-ready格式。适用场景广泛，涵盖装修前规划、房地产虚拟staging、租赁空间优化以及个人家居灵感收集。
items.quote: Roomzine 为您的房间制作一份精美的杂志页面，包含改造前后的对比、配色方案、编辑文案和购物清单。
items.titleZh: Show HN：Roomzine —— 把你的房间照片变成一份重新设计的杂志
